title: Researchers Dispute Whether AI Has Passed Turing Test
source_used: Mirage News (carrying a University of Canterbury release)
key_facts: Researchers at the University of Canterbury (New Zealand), philosopher Diane Proudfoot, PhD student Sharon Temtsin and Professor Christoph Bartneck, argue many 'Turing Tests' do not follow Turing's original design.
They say the five-minute limit and the 30 percent fooled rule were not Turing's rules; he envisaged an open-ended three-player game.
They ran what they say is the first experiment of Turing's original design, using GPT-4-Turbo.
36 of 37 participants (97 percent) correctly identified GPT-4-Turbo; 33 (89 percent) took longer than five minutes; the average chat lasted 14 minutes, the longest 46.
The authors say no large language model has yet been shown to pass the original design, but newer models may perform differently.
quote_evidence: Of 37 participants, 36 correctly identified GPT-4-Turbo - a recognition rate of 97%.
The researchers stress that their findings do not show that all current or future AI models would fail.
why_it_matters_hint: Claims that AI has 'passed the Turing Test' depend on which version of the test is used.
notes: Mirage News carries a University of Canterbury press release; the university is credited as source. Study used an older model.
